questions.question: Which chapter introduces the Transformer?
options: Chapter 15, Language models and the Transformer
questions.answer: Chapter 15, Language models and the Transformer
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 is titled 'Language models and the Transformer' (p.445). Chapter 14 is text classification, 16 text generation, 9 ConvNet architecture patterns.

questions.question: Chapter 13 starts on printed page 351. On which PDF page does it start, given the offset of 24?
Which chapters cover computer vision?
questions.answer: Chapters 8-12: image classification, ConvNet architecture patterns, interpreting ConvNets, image segmentation, object detection.

questions.question: Why do chapters 2 and 3 come before any application chapters?
questions.answer: They provide the mathematical building blocks (tensors, gradients, backpropagation) and the frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX, Keras) every later chapter relies on.
questions.explanation: The order on this page shows a bottom-up design: foundations first, then applications.

questions.question: Which chapter would you read to learn a step-by-step process for tackling any ML project?
options: Chapter 6, The universal workflow of machine learning
Chapter 7, A deep dive on Keras
Chapter 18, Best practices for the real world
questions.answer: Chapter 6, The universal workflow of machine learning
questions.explanation: Chapter 6 (p.195) is the workflow chapter. Chapter 5 covers fundamentals like generalization, 7 is Keras in depth, 18 is real-world best practices.

questions.question: Which part of the book are you most interested in, and have you planned to cover chapters 1-7 first?
questions.explanation: Chapters 1-7 are prerequisites for the later, more modular chapters.
